title: GesBench: When and Where Do Multimodal Language Models Perceive Social Meaning?
abstract: arXiv:2610.15129v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human social perception is incremental: we infer intent before an utterance is complete, revise our interpretation as new cues arrive, and attend to specific facial, gestural, or prosodic signals that shape social meaning. Current multimodal LLM benchmarks largely evaluate final-answer understanding over complete episodes, rewarding post-hoc recognition of social meaning rather than the unfolding perception required for real-time interaction. Drawing on interactionally embedded Gestalt principles of multimodal human communication, we introduce GesBench: a human-grounded benchmark for cue-level social perception in multimodal LLMs. GesBench uses cumulative sub-utterance clips to measure when models form stable interpretations of speaker intention and social affordance, and human gaze-guided corruption to evaluate whether regions attended by humans are functionally important for model judgments. translated_title: GesBench：多模态语言模型何时以及在哪里感知社会意义？
translated_abstract: 人类的社会感知是渐进式的：我们在话语尚未结束时就能推断意图，随着新线索的到来修正我们的理解，并关注那些塑造社会意义的特定面部、手势或韵律信号。当前的多模态大语言模型基准主要评估对完整情境的最终答案理解，奖励对社会意义的事后识别，而非实时交互所需的动态展开式感知。基于多模态人类交流中交互嵌入的格式塔原则，我们提出了GesBench：一个以人类为基础、针对多模态大语言模型线索级社会感知的基准。GesBench使用累积式亚话语片段来测量模型何时形成对说话者意图和社会可供性的稳定解释，并通过人类注视引导的损坏实验来评估人类所关注的区域对模型判断是否具有功能性重要性。该基准基于超过6000个话语级片段构建……
tldr: GesBench是一个以人类认知为基础的多模态大语言模型社会感知评估基准，通过累积式亚话语片段测量模型形成稳定社会解释的时间点，并通过人类注视引导的损坏实验验证人类关注区域对模型判断的功能重要性。
